clue.text: Lend to dame, to keep-what a wonderful thing

parts.note: to lend is to give as a loan
DBE, Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire, is the title a dame holds
to keep something is to hold it

explanation.surface: Someone lends to an elderly lady who will keep the money, and marvels at it.
explanation.walkthrough: DBE is the British honour that makes a woman a Dame.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of astonishment used on presenting something remarkable.

clue.text: Not a religious poem

definitions.meaning: ... people are not clergy, so non-religious in that sense

explanation.definitionFit: Lay means non-clerical as an adjective and a ballad or short narrative poem as a noun.

clue.text: One no longer young given notice last month

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
ult., ultimo, is the old business abbreviation for last month

explanation.surface: Someone getting on in years was handed a notice in the previous month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' merely links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up person has left youth behind, so this is a fair synonym for a grown person.

clue.text: Best friends perhaps went ahead in polar transport

parts.note: dogs are called man's best friend, the 'perhaps' marking an example
led means went in front

explanation.surface: Close companions took the lead on an Arctic expedition vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled drawn by a team of huskies is the classic means of travel across polar snow.

clue.text: Supply to French department is in balance

parts.note: to equip is to supply with what is needed
Oise is a department of northern France

explanation.surface: Getting provisions to a region of France keeps things even.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' joins the pieces and 'is in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipoise is a state of equilibrium, an even balance of forces.

clue.text: Midlands town said to have ropy bits

indicators.note: said signals that the town's name is heard, not spelt

parts.note: Oakham is the county town of Rutland, in England's East Midlands

explanation.surface: A town in central England is reputed to own pieces of rope.
explanation.walkthrough: OAKHAM is a small market town in Rutland, England's smallest county.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakum is loose fibre teased from old ropes, used to caulk ships' seams.

clue.text: I'd lifted cap's peak to factor

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the letters are turned to read upwards

parts.note: taken as its letters, the apostrophe dropped
the visor is the peak of a cap

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have raised the brim of a cap for a reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns ID into DI.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic a divisor is a number that divides another exactly, that is, a factor of it.

clue.text: Very excited, seeing mother return

indicators.note: return signals reading the word backwards

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: Someone is overjoyed to see their mum come home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns DAM into MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad can mean wildly enthusiastic or frenzied, as in mad with joy.

clue.text: Telegraph staff needed to master the long and short: of it

definitions.text: Telegraph staff needed to master the long and short: of it

parts.words: Telegraph staff needed to master the long and short: of it
parts.note: the surface is about newspaper staff and the gist of a story; read literally, telegraph operators must learn a system of long and short signals

explanation.surface: Employees of the Telegraph newspaper had to grasp the essentials of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Telegraph is a British newspaper; the italic name misleads towards it rather than the telegraph instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The system transmits letters as dashes and dots, long and short signals that telegraphists had to learn.

clue.text: Nonsensical result of bigamy?

definitions.meaning: 'dutch' is old slang for wife, so a bigamist has two of them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old dutch' is cockney slang for a wife, so two wives makes a jokey second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means incomprehensible jargon, and literally two wives in the old cockney slang.

clue.text: Baby in Izmir one's anxious to change

parts.note: young means offspring, a baby animal
Izmir is a city in Turkey, so one of its people is a Turk

explanation.surface: An infant in the Turkish city of Izmir is impatient for things to be different.
explanation.definitionFit: A Young Turk is an impatient reformer, after the early twentieth-century Turkish revolutionary party.

clue.text: Connoisseurship is not entirely an admirable quality

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a virtue is a good or admirable quality

explanation.surface: Being an expert judge of art falls a little short of being a real merit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is not entirely' cuts the final E off VIRTUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtu means knowledge of and taste for fine objects of art, that is, connoisseurship.

clue.text: Pet beat wings, cutting through doorway

parts.note: a cat is a typical household pet
to flap is to beat the wings

explanation.surface: A pet bird flaps its wings as it shoots through the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat flap is a small hinged opening cut through a door for a pet to use.

clue.text: Flora on this farm in 'cheerless condition

definitions.meaning: Flora Poste is the heroine of Stella Gibbons's comic novel set on a gloomy Sussex farm
poor consolation that offers little real help

explanation.walkthrough: Flora looks like plant life; she is the heroine of a 1932 English comic novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means scant consolation, and also names the farm in Stella Gibbons's novel.

clue.text: Wrongly issue forged medal — one's accepted

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so one piece goes inside another
forged means made falsely, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: one is I, and the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A fake decoration is passed off as genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' looks like it describes the medal, but it is the anagram signal, turning MEDAL into MDEAL before 'accepted' takes in the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdeal is to hand out cards wrongly, so to issue them incorrectly.

clue.text: Half-heartedly cut and ran

indicators.note: half the heart goes, so one of the two central letters is dropped

parts.note: to lop is to cut off, past tense lopped

explanation.surface: Someone half-hearted about trimming a tree ran off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-heartedly' removes one of the twin P letters at the centre of LOPPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long bounding strides, so loped is a past tense of running.

clue.text: Ceremony needs a severe hairstyle

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial display
dour means stern or severe

explanation.surface: A formal occasion calls for a strict hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link word joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a style with the hair swept up high off the forehead.

clue.text: One's joined woman's club as — writer.

parts.note: one is I, and the 's is read as 'is'
her is the possessive for a woman
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A man joins a women's club as its official writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joined' and 'as' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood was an English novelist, author of Goodbye to Berlin.

clue.text: Applause given to batting success — good balance, head right down

parts.note: a hand is a round of applause
in cricket a stand is a long partnership between two batters

explanation.surface: A cricketer's good innings earns applause, with fine poise and head bowed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a STAND is a productive partnership between two batters.
explanation.definitionFit: Balancing on the hands with the head nearest the ground and feet in the air is a handstand.

clue.text: Admit effect of addiction to, soaps?

definitions.meaning: to own up or confess the truth
jokingly, what using too much soap would do to you

explanation.walkthrough: Soaps looks like television dramas, but read literally means bars of soap.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess fully is to own up, while literally overusing soap would leave you spotless.

clue.text: Result of eruption about to engulf tree

indicators.note: to engulf means to surround, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: ca. is circa, about
the alder is a tree

explanation.surface: Lava from an eruption is about to swallow a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads like 'on the point of', but 'about' gives CA (circa) and 'to engulf' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A caldera is a large crater formed when a volcano collapses after an eruption.

clue.text: Prison ships

definitions.meaning: a group of ships sailing together

explanation.walkthrough: The Fleet Prison stood beside the River Fleet in London until 1844.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fleet was a notorious London debtors' prison, and a navy is a body of ships.

clue.text: Strange old fellow raised to be king

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: to reign is to rule as king

explanation.surface: An odd old man was elevated to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns OF into FO.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign can mean alien or unfamiliar, so strange.

clue.text: Spots travelling salesmen finishing early

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving about, so the letters are rearranged
stopping early means the last letter of salesmen is lost

explanation.surface: Commercial travellers knock off early because of a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing early' drops the last N of SALESMEN; 'travelling' rearranges SALESME.
explanation.definitionFit: The illness is known for its rash, so spots stands for it by association.

clue.text: Character shown in extremities by Sophocles

definitions.text: Character shown in extremities by Sophocles

parts.words: Character shown in extremities by Sophocles
parts.note: the Greek dramatist's name begins and ends with the same letter, which in Greek is written with this character

explanation.walkthrough: Character looks like a figure in a play by Sophocles; it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the Greek letter S, which opens and closes the name of the Greek playwright.

clue.text: Exaggerate how much time one's been given

definitions.text: how much time one's been given
definitions.meaning: a prison sentence, a term inside

explanation.definitionFit: To stretch the truth is to exaggerate, and a stretch is slang for a prison sentence.

clue.text: Stomach mind-blowing experience with drug

parts.note: a trip is a hallucinatory experience
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone's gut reaction to a hallucination brought on by drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is the stomach lining of a cow or sheep, eaten as food.

clue.text: Gas ring brought to district

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
a zone is an area or district

explanation.surface: A gas ring has been delivered to a local area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought to' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen, a gas with three atoms per molecule.

clue.text: Delighted as wedding finally formally approved

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of wedding

parts.note: ratified means formally approved

explanation.surface: The couple are delighted that their marriage was at last officially sanctioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be gratified is to be pleased or satisfied, so delighted.

clue.text: Mark has to serve time

parts.note: to do time is to serve a sentence, so do means serve

explanation.surface: A man called Mark has to serve a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot is a small mark or spot.

clue.text: Raced, say, to peak

indicators.note: say signals the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: tore means rushed or raced

explanation.surface: Someone sped up to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky peak or hilltop.

clue.text: Desertion of sailor and soldier Cossacks captured

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: captured means held inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant
the Don Cossacks are men of the River Don

explanation.surface: A navy man and an army man deserted after Cossacks took them prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cossacks of the River Don are read as 'Don men'; 'of' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandonment is the act of deserting or leaving behind.
